blocks.text: Tzetzes, Chil. 8, Hist. 173. Scholia on Oppian and on Nicander's Ther.

On the meleagrides [guinea fowl] compare what SCHNEIDER said on Aelian's History of Animals IV, 42, to which he added some things in the Appendix to the Commentaries on the Remains of the Books of Frederick II and the chapters of Albertus Magnus on the art of hunting with birds, Leipzig 1789, p. 163. That the meleagrides are the Numidae of Linnaeus (Syst. Nat. vol. I, part II, p. 744, 13th ed.), Perlhühner [guinea fowl], was shown, following Perrault, by PALLAS in Spicil. Zoolog. III, p. 13 ff.

Yet the opinion of J. D. Michaelis in the Supplements, vol. I, p. 228, does not seem to be dismissed: that ברברים, or, as it is written in 14 of Kennicott's codices, ברבורים, are animals of the fields, forests and deserts which we usually catch by hunting, as opposed to domestic [II, 708] ones, from the Chaldee בָּרָא, Syriac ܒܪܐ, Arabic بَرّ [barr], field, desert. What he added to commend this opinion should be read in his own work.

There is nothing about Cadmus in that passage of Strabo, as Michaelis observed, loc. cit. p. 227, who quoted the Greek words themselves; and he should certainly be compared on what Bochart adduces here.
